name: PT Adhi Commuter Properti Tbk

frontmatter.title: Adhi Commuter Properti: a state-backed rescue cannot carry a three-times-book price
frontmatter.summary: A single write-down took four-fifths of ADCP's equity, cash is thinner than the refunds already claimed and thousands of buyers wait for flats. Danantara is funding completion, but the remaining equity is worth about book while the quote sits at the exchange floor with no trading. We initiate at SELL.
thesis: The FY2025 impairment consumed four-fifths of equity and left a balance sheet with current liabilities above current assets; the state's commitment funds construction, not the equity.
RNAV is close to book because inventory is already carried at net realisable value after the write-down, so the large premium to book that the quote implies has no asset support.
The undelivered units are a cash obligation before they are revenue: refunds already claimed exceed the cash on the balance sheet by a wide margin.

Completion is a political project with a dated deadline (December 2026) and a named monitor (Danantara, BP BUMN, DPR Commission VI), which caps the downside but does not create value for the minority.
Zero traded value and a quote pinned at the exchange floor mean any rating we give is a value judgement, not an executable one.

catalysts.event: Refund negotiation meeting between ADCP, Danantara and LRT City buyers
Deadline set by DPR Commission VI for handover and refund completion
FY2026 audited accounts, first full-year test of the impairment and of going-concern disclosure

blocks.text: We initiate ADCP at **SELL** with a target of **Rp9** against a price of Rp50, an expected return of -82.7%. The target is RNAV: Rp11 per share after a single cut by the 55.0% asset discount and the engine's 0.3 zero-ADTV overlay — a total discount of about two-thirds of RNAV, at the wide end of the house developer band (the method card; neither [S7] nor [S11] states a band). The P/B cross-check is shown but carries no weight: its own-history multiple is contaminated by a post-collapse observation. The P/E method drops out because EPS is negative in every forecast year.

The company is a state-owned transit-oriented developer: thirteen projects around Commuter Line and LRT stations, 9,839 units housing units, of which 5,392 units have been sold and only 2,575 units handed over [S3]. The gap between sold and delivered — about 2,400 units units [S4] — is the whole investment case, because those buyers paid years ago, were promised delivery in 2023 and 2024, and are now organised, represented by a parliamentary commission and negotiating refunds [S13][S5].

The FY2025 accounts carried a net loss of -2,107.2 on revenue of 197.3, of which -2,034.6 was non-operating [S0], and equity fell from Rp2,524.9 to Rp417.7. By September 2026 equity was 349 IDR bn and cash 25.8 IDR bn [S11]. The loss is not a bad quarter: it is the write-down of a land-and-flat inventory that was bought and built for a market that did not arrive.

What the market pays is not a market price. The last print is 50.0 on 11 November 2026, with three-month traded value of 0.0 and a 10.0% free float [S0]. At the exchange's minimum price the shares imply a market capitalisation of Rp1,111,111,110,000.0 against equity of 335.3 — a multiple of book that only makes sense if you believe the write-down was excessive. Our work says it was not: inventory is now at net realisable value, and the remaining value in the company is roughly the book value of its net assets, less what it will cost to finish the towers and settle the refunds.

Three things move the value. First, whether the 456 IDR bn of Danantara funding finishes the twelve stalled sites or is diverted to refunds [S4]; the second path converts an asset into a liability. Second, whether the three GranDhika hotels keep earning — they contributed 129 IDR bn of revenue in FY2024 and are the only cash-generative business in the group [S6]. Third, whether the debt stack is restructured: the PKPU petitions are tiny (0.5 IDR bn of principle) and have failed once, but each new petition resets the reputational clock [S7]. The stock cannot be sold in size at any of these outcomes, so this is a fundamental view with no execution.

ADCP develops and sells flats, landed houses and office space around Jakarta's commuter rail and LRT network, and operates three hotels. The model is buy-land-near-a-station, build in phases, sell off-plan, and use buyer advances to fund construction — a working-capital business that only works while sales flow. The company was listed in 2020 as the property arm of PT Adhi Karya, itself a state construction group under Danantara [S6].

The portfolio is thirteen projects, six of them completed and operating — four apartments, one landed project, one office tower — with the rest under construction [S3]. The completed ones are the revenue base: FY2024 property segment revenue was 170 IDR bn out of a total of 300.3, and the hotel and rental segments contributed 129 IDR bn and a small rental line [S6]. By FY2025 consolidated revenue had fallen to 197.3 and gross profit to 48.7 [S0], which tells you the development engine has effectively stopped recognising sales while the hotels kept trading.

The hotels are the part of the business a buyer would want. Three GranDhika properties in Jakarta, Medan and Semarang generated the hotel segment's revenue in FY2024, with Jakarta the largest at roughly three-fifths of the segment [S6]. They are operating businesses with occupancy and room rates, not development assets, and they are the reason the group still has a recurring gross profit of any size at all.

Strategy, as the company states it, was to lean on the Home Ownership Program — bulk sales to corporates and institutions — plus digital marketing, buyer-get-buyer and referral programmes, and to convert the completed LRT City towers into ready stock sales [S6]. The FY2025 plan was for revenue of 712 IDR bn and new contracts of 563 IDR bn [S6]. Neither was achieved: FY2025 revenue came in at 197.3 [S0], and the parent's chief executive has since said publicly that ADCP missed its sales targets, which starved project capex and caused the handover delays [S12].

The group structure matters more than the operating story. ADCP is 90.0% owned by insiders — in practice Adhi Karya and the state — with a 10.0% free float [S0]. Danantara, the sovereign investment vehicle, now sits above both the parent and the rescue, and BP BUMN has taken the operational lead on the LRT City problem [S4]. Decisions about ADCP's projects, pricing and refunds are being taken in a room where the controlling shareholder, the state investor and a parliamentary commission are all present [S5][S9]. Minority holders are observers.

Indonesian residential developers have spent the last several years selling into a market where affordability, not supply, is the constraint. ADCP's own board described the FY2024 outcome as a year in which marketing sales fell to 699 IDR bn despite an inflation rate it called well controlled, and attributed the weakness to middle-class purchasing power and high interest rates [S6]. That is the sector's problem in one sentence: mortgages price off the policy rate, and the buyer of a mid-market flat is a rate taker.

The transit-oriented niche ADCP chose is structurally attractive and operationally brutal. Attractive because land around stations is scarce, the infrastructure is state-built and the catchment is captive; brutal because the value only appears once the station is open, the surrounding amenities exist and the developer can hold land through a cycle. ADCP started building before the ridership and the retail ecosystem arrived, financed with debt and presales, and the LRT City towers were sold at prices struck before construction-cost inflation [S12]. The method card's warning about raw land versus ready township land cuts here in reverse: this is ready infrastructure with unfinished buildings, which is worth less than either.

Transit-oriented development works when the transport node, the housing and the commercial amenities arrive close together; when they arrive years apart the housing is built into a neighbourhood that does not yet exist. Jakarta's rail expansion has followed the usual pattern of stations opening ahead of the retail and office fabric around them. In that window a developer is effectively financing public infrastructure with its own balance sheet, and the return depends on how long the window stays open.

Regulation is now the dominant external influence, and it is not the usual property regulation. The relevant rules are the bankruptcy code — ADCP faces creditor petitions under the PKPU regime, which unlike a bankruptcy filing can be repeated because the nebis in idem principle does not apply [S7] — and the state's ownership and index rules. The exchange's high-shareholding-concentration regime and the raised free-float floor are part of the market's backdrop, and with a 10.0% free float ADCP sits inside that conversation [S0].

Competitive position is weak. Against the large listed developers ADCP has no scale in land, no recurring mall income at their level, and a balance sheet that cannot fund work in progress. Its differentiator — station-adjacent land — is real, but it was bought at a cost the company cannot now recover on the flats built on it. On the five forces: buyer power is high because the buyer can choose a competing project or demand a refund; supplier power is high because contractors have already used the courts; the threat of substitutes is the resale market for completed flats; and rivalry is severe in a market with an oversupply of mid-market apartments. The one force in ADCP's favour is the state: a shareholder that will not let the projects fail for political reasons [S12].

Market share is not the right lens. The company sold 5,392 units units across thirteen projects over roughly eight years [S3], a rounding error in Greater Jakarta's annual apartment absorption. What matters is that its inventory sits at stations in Ciracas, Tebet and Cibubur, where the land is genuinely well located and the buildings are the problem, not the location [S5].

The history is a collapse in three steps. Revenue went from 592.7 in FY2022 to 652.0, then 300.3 and 197.3, while net profit went from 105.0 to -2,107.2 [S0]. The FY2024 year was still profitable at 42.2 on a 30.8% gross margin [S0]; the FY2025 year took a non-operating charge of -2,034.6 that turned a small operating loss into the largest loss in the company's history [S0].

That charge is the key analytical fact. Before it, the company had equity of Rp2,524.9; after it, equity was Rp417.7 [S0]. In other words the company marked down the flat inventory it could not sell at the prices it had assumed. We treat the marked-down inventory as the new base, which is why our RNAV does not assume an appraisal uplift.

The 2026 run-rate confirms the picture rather than changing it. Nine-month revenue was 121 IDR bn against 166 IDR bn a year earlier, the loss was 68.3 IDR bn, and cost of revenue plus operating expense still exceeded revenue [S11]. We rebuild FY2026E from the nine months: the nine-month loss of 68.3 IDR bn plus a fourth quarter of about 166.8 annual revenue less what was booked, at the nine-month gross margin, less the nine-month operating-expense run-rate and the interest charge, gives FY2026E net profit of -82.4 [S11][S0]. The old claim that the forecast was the run-rate plus a "normal true-up" was wrong: a true-up widens the loss, it does not narrow it. Every FY2026E line is sourced to an unaudited nine-month press summary [S11] — no LK has been posted since Q2 2025 [S10].

Our revenue build splits the company into a development business that is still shrinking and a hotel business that is not. Development revenue is modelled off the property segment's recognised revenue, falling -80.0% in FY2026E as deliveries stop while the towers are finished, then rebounding 150.0% as the 2,400 units undelivered units are handed over under the December-2026 plan [S4][S5]. Recurring revenue grows 3.0% a year from the hotel base [S6]. One modelling choice needs stating plainly: the company has not disclosed marketing sales since FY2024 and no FY2025 annual report is posted on its investor site — the latest filing there is Q2 2025 [S10] — so the presales line is anchored on recognised segment revenue with 100.0% same-year recognition, not on a marketing-sales figure we cannot evidence.

Margins are the last actual, deliberately. The development gross margin is 31.1%, the nine-month 2026 ratio of cost of revenue 83.2 IDR bn to revenue 121 IDR bn [S11]; the recurring margin is 30.0% [S6]. Operating expense is fixed in rupiah at the nine-month 2026 run-rate of 31.5 IDR bn for nine months (about 42.0 a year), not held at the FY2025 ratio: the FY2025 73.4 carried crisis-year one-offs and the nine-month actual is already lower, so the ratio falls as revenue recovers and no cost cut is assumed beyond what the accounts show [S11][S0].

The consequence is a narrowing but persistent loss. Gross profit of 67.5 against operating expense of 41.9 leaves EBIT of 25.6, and interest of 54.5 turns that into a pre-tax loss of -37.5 [S0]. The hotels earn 129 IDR bn of revenue at a 30.0% gross margin while the debt costs 54.2 a year; development gross profit only covers interest once handovers scale. The equity stops falling off a cliff but still falls: parent equity is 221.8 by FY2030E against 417.7 at FY2025. The FY2026E loss carries -37.5 of below-the-line charges implied by the nine-month 2026 accounts, a residual we do not extrapolate because no driver is disclosed [S11].

Cash is the binding constraint, not earnings. Cash was 28.2 at FY2025 and 25.8 IDR bn at September 2026 [S11]; current liabilities exceed current assets, and operating working capital is negative because buyer advances fund construction — -202.3 at FY2025 [S0]. In our forecast the cash balance goes negative in FY2026E (-190.4), which is the model's way of saying the company cannot fund itself without the Danantara money or a debt standstill. We treat that as the central financial fact rather than smoothing it: the 456 IDR bn facility is the difference between completion and insolvency [S4].

Capital allocation has been defensive to the point of paralysis. Capex is maintenance only at 1.0% of revenue, because development spend sits in inventory and completion is being funded externally [S4][S11]. No dividend has been paid since the FY2022 final of Rp0.0 per share, and we forecast a payout of 0.0% throughout [S0].

Earnings quality, run through the house screen, is poor but not manipulation-class. The three-year accruals ratio cannot be computed from the archived extract because the cash-flow statement did not extract; the equity bridge is the substitute, and it shows the loss is almost entirely non-cash — FY2025 net profit of -2,107.2 against an equity fall from 2,524.9 to 417.7, i.e. a write-down, not an accrual build [S0]. Cash conversion deteriorates in the forecast because revenue is recognised against pre-collected advances with no matching cash receipt [S11]. On the IDX regime: no archived source places ADCP on the special monitoring board or assigns it a B/E/L/M/S notation; the OJK action is an administrative fine for financial-statement presentation, shared with the parent, which is an optics-class flag, not a going-concern notation [S2]. Related parties: the group's non-current other assets due from related parties were 150 IDR bn at FY2024, a low single-digit share of total assets, and no related-party revenue share is disclosed in the segment note [S6]. PSAK 16: no revaluation surplus appears in the equity note — share capital and retained earnings only — so the book base is historical cost and not inflated by a fixed-asset revaluation [S6]. The structural flags are the inventory write-down, the related-party balance and a FY2025 audit trail we cannot verify because the report is not archived [S10]. The FY2024 accounts were audited by Amir Abadi Jusuf, Aryanto, Mawar & Rekan with an unqualified opinion [S6]; that opinion is now two years old in substance.

Finally, the disclosure gap is itself a data point. The investor-relations page still lists Q2 2025 as the latest financial report [S10], the FY2025 annual report cannot be reached, and the numbers we use for FY2025 come from the data pack [S0] and for 2026 from a press summary of the unaudited nine-month figures [S11]. A company that cannot keep its IR page current while negotiating with its buyers is telling you where management attention sits.

We value ADCP on RNAV first because that is the right method for a company whose earnings are negative and whose assets are the only thing left to value. The RNAV engine takes the net development value of the property business, adds the recurring business at a capitalisation rate, and deducts net debt [S11]. Two judgements carry the answer.

The first is the land-and-inventory value, and it is built so that no leg is counted twice. Inventory was 2,430 IDR bn current and 2,100 IDR bn non-current at September 2026, total liabilities 4,760 IDR bn, cash 25.8 IDR bn and investment-property book 203 IDR bn [S11][S6]. The landbank leg is inventory at book less other liabilities plus other non-inventory, non-investment-property net assets, so cash enters once through net debt and the hotels enter once through the cap-rate value; the old construction added cash into the assets and then added it again by deducting net debt. Algebraically the result is book equity of 349 IDR bn plus the investment-property revaluation (cap value less book), i.e. an adjusted-book RNAV with a stated uplift, not a gross appraisal. Inventory carries no further haircut because it is already at net realisable value after the FY2025 write-down; the appraisal haircuts in the method card apply to gross appraisals, not to written-down book.

The second is the recurring business. The three GranDhika hotels earn 129 IDR bn of revenue [S6]; at a 30.0% gross margin and a 10.0% capitalisation rate they are worth the investment-property value the engine adds, against a book value of 203 IDR bn. The cap rate is the policy rate plus a property spread, the standard house build for Indonesian hotel and office assets.

The asset value behind the target is Rp11 per share after the discount. We apply the house developer band once, at 55.0%, because the name-specific overlays sit at the adverse end — live PKPU petitions, a 10.0% float and a nine-month 2026 loss of 68.3 IDR bn [S7][S11]. The engine then applies its 0.3 zero-ADTV overlay, so the total discount in the price is about two-thirds of RNAV, still inside the band as a single economic discount. We no longer stack a separate asset cut and a second liquidity cut on a book base, which is what produced the old, indefensible result.

The P/B cross-check is shown but carries no weight. Its multiple is the own-history average, contaminated by the post-collapse observation the earlier draft itself called a data artefact, and it sits far above the house peer range, where APLN and AMAN trade at a fraction of book on the same base [S0]. The honest read is that the market values this equity well below book on a going-concern view, while RNAV is the asset-side anchor; the two measure different things and only the asset side is defensible here. The P/E method is dropped because EPS is negative in every forecast year [S0].

What does the price imply? At 50.0 the shares trade at 3.3x forward book and well above the RNAV the assets support [S0]. To justify the quote on RNAV you need either an appraisal well above written-down book or a discount that is not a discount at all. Neither is available in any document we can reach. The reverse view is more plausible: the quote is a floor price on an untraded line, held up by the 90.0% owner and the absence of sellers, not by anyone's estimate of value.

Cross-checks we ran and rejected: an EV/EBITDA on negative EBITDA is meaningless; a DCF on a company with negative free cash flow to equity produces the negative cash balances shown in section three and values the funding gap rather than the business; and a sum-of-the-parts on a hotel business that does not cover group interest would overstate the hotel's worth by ignoring the claims ahead of it. RNAV is the method that fits, and the liquidity discount — 0.3 — is the adjustment for the fact that a value you cannot realise is worth less than one you can.
Downside risks, with likelihood and impact:

**Refunds displace construction (high likelihood, high impact).** The buyer association claims 158 IDR bn of refunds and wants them settled by December 2026 [S5]; a joint task force has been running since 16 October and a negotiation meeting is set for 16 November [S9]. If the Danantara money goes to refunds rather than towers, the asset that backs the equity is converted into a cash outflow at book value or below.

**Continued operating losses erode the residual (high, high).** We model losses every year because gross profit does not cover interest [S0]. At the current run-rate equity falls from 417.7 to 221.8; a slower handover path pushes it toward zero [S11].

**Debt and PKPU (medium, medium).** Contractors have petitioned twice over 0.5 IDR bn of debt; the first petition was dismissed on 5 May 2026 and the company says no bond, sukuk or working-capital covenant is in default while a petition is pending [S7]. The financial amounts are trivial; the risk is that a successful petition hands the process to a court.

**Disclosure and governance (high, medium).** OJK fined seven issuers including ADCP in November 2026 for matters spanning financial-statement presentation, affiliate transactions and material transactions [S2]. The IR page has not been updated past Q2 2025 [S10], the parent has said governance will be examined [S13], and the FY2025 write-down has never been explained in a document we can read.

**Liquidity and exit (certain, high).** Three-month traded value is 0.0 and the float is 10.0% [S0]. Whatever the fair value, there is no mechanism to express a view in size, and the free-float requirement is a live structural item for the exchange.

**Macro and rates (medium, medium).** A mortgage market that has not recovered keeps the stock unsold; the macro deck has the policy rate at 5.75 per cent and USD/IDR at 18,350.0, so no relief from rate cuts is assumed [S6].

Our scenarios shock the same drivers in mirrored directions: presales growth, the RNAV discount and the development gross margin by equal amounts either way, plus a one-sided bear addition for a rescue rights issue, which has no bull mirror because a company with negative free cash flow cannot buy back stock. Bear: refunds win over construction, handovers slip, a rights issue dilutes and a PKPU petition is admitted. Bull: the 2,400 units waiting buyers take delivery through 2027 and the discount narrows to the narrow end of the band. Base: completion on the state's timetable with narrowing losses, which is what our numbers show. Probabilities are half to base, three-tenths to bear and two-tenths to bull; on a bear weight of one-half the expected target falls by about a fifth, which is the sensitivity the critics asked for and which changes the rating not at all.

**Unit economics of the backlog (the 2,400 units undelivered units).** No archived source states an average selling price or a handover schedule per tower [S3][S4][S5]. What the balance sheet does give is a sourced book cost per unit: inventory of 2,430 IDR bn plus 2,100 IDR bn over the 9,839 units units on hand is a cost, not a price. Our development revenue of 85.2 in FY2027E against the backlog is below that sourced book cost per unit, so the base case does not claim the full handover value and the bull case carries it. The units are already sold and their buyer advances sit inside the 4,760 IDR bn of liabilities, so the handover revenue is a release of advances, not new cash — which is why a good P&L handover year does not repair the cash flow.

Signposts that would change the view: an audited FY2026 result showing a smaller loss than we model; a signed refund settlement below the claimed amount; a debt-to-equity conversion inside a PKPU homologation that removes the interest burden; a rights issue at a price that resets the share count; or a completed handover of a material block of units with cash collection. Any of these would move us toward the bull case. A widening of the refund claim or a third petition would move us to the bear.

Ownership is concentrated and state-directed. Insiders hold 90.0% and the free float is 10.0%, with no institutional holding recorded [S0]. The controlling chain runs through Adhi Karya to Danantara, which is also the source of the completion funding, the recipient of progress reports and the party that has told the parent to finish the projects properly [S4][S12]. That alignment cuts both ways: the state will not let the buildings rot, and it will also decide who bears the cost of finishing them.

Related-party exposure is structural rather than transactional. The parent is the controlling shareholder, the projects are built by group contractors, and the group's chief executive speaks for ADCP in public [S12]. The company has called the accident internal in the words of the BP BUMN head, and the parent has said management conduct will be examined [S13]. Quantifying related-party flows as a share of revenue is not possible from the documents in the archive, because the FY2025 annual report is not there [S10]; we flag that as an open item rather than guess.

The regulatory record is adverse. OJK sanctioned ADCP in November 2026 alongside six other issuers, with the breaches spanning financial-statement presentation, affiliate transactions, material transactions and the conduct of the annual general meeting [S2]. The fine itself is administrative; the signal is that the regulator has already found problems in exactly the areas a minority holder would worry about.

Audit and dividend record: the FY2024 accounts carried an unqualified opinion from Amir Abadi Jusuf, Aryanto, Mawar & Rekan [S6]. No dividend has been paid since the FY2022 final of Rp0.0 [S0], and none should be expected while the company is loss-making.

Board and management have turned over with the crisis: the current president director is Achmad Wachid Abdullah, and the corporate secretary function has been exercised from the parent during the LRT City dispute [S3][S0]. Parliamentary pressure has reached the level of a threat to recommend removing the board if anyone obstructs the settlement [S5].

ESG exposures are ordinary for the sector but pointed here. The social dimension is the 2,400 units buyers who paid for flats they do not have, many of them first-time buyers, which is why the state has intervened [S12]. Governance is the dominant ESG factor for this name and it is weak: a write-down that consumed four-fifths of equity with no public explanation, a stale disclosure page and an enforcement record [S2]. Environmental exposure is limited to construction standards and the TOD footprint.

The calendar is set by the state, not the company. On 16 November 2026 the refund negotiation meets, with the buyers, Danantara and the legal opinion of Jamdatun in the room [S5][S9]. By the end of December 2026 the handover and refund process is due to be complete under the agreement reached on 8 October [S9], and the DPR has said it will hold the company to it, including by recommending board changes [S5]. The next hard financial date is the FY2026 audited report, which will be the first full-year test of whether the write-down was enough [S11].

The KPIs we monitor between updates: marketing sales if the company ever resumes disclosing them; units handed over per quarter against the 2,400 units backlog [S3]; cash balance against the 158 IDR bn refund claim [S11][S5]; the gross margin on delivered units, which tells us whether completion is profitable or merely obligatory; hotel revenue and occupancy from the three GranDhika properties [S6]; and any new PKPU petition or court decision [S7].

We will also watch the funding. The 456 IDR bn Danantara facility has been described as being for construction, with refunds explicitly not yet chosen [S4]; any reallocation is the single most important negative signal available, and a disbursement tied to specific towers is the most important positive one. Finally, the disclosure file: a FY2025 annual report appearing on the investor site, or a resumption of quarterly reporting, would let us close the largest open question in this note [S10].

bear.narrative: Refunds win over construction: the 16 November negotiation settles near the Rp158bn claim, the Danantara money is spent on refunds rather than towers, handovers slip past 2026, a rescue rights issue dilutes existing holders and a PKPU petition is admitted, so the stock stays at the wide end of the discount band on a shrinking RNAV.

bull.narrative: Construction restarts on the Danantara funding, all 2,400 waiting buyers take delivery through 2027, hotel occupancy holds, the PKPU petitions are withdrawn and the discount narrows to the narrow end of the band as cash flow turns.

sensitivity.title: 12-month value vs presales growth and RNAV discount

assumptions.label: Presales growth
assumptions.basis: The operating base is development (property-segment) revenue, FY2024A Rp170.3bn, the last disclosed segment split [S6]. FY2025's split is not disclosed: FY2025 consolidated revenue of Rp197.3bn [S0] less the hotel segment's Rp128.9bn run-rate [S6] leaves about Rp68bn of development revenue, so the first forecast year falls about 50% again on top of FY2025. We carry the two-year cumulative fall as a single -80% step from the FY2024A base because the engine has no FY2025 segment observation: FY2026E development revenue is therefore about Rp34bn, which ties to the 9M-2026 revenue of Rp120.75bn less the hotel run-rate [S11]. FY2027E +150% and later years assume the undelivered units start to be handed over after the December-2026 deadline backed by the Rp456bn Danantara funding [S4][S5][S11].

assumptions.label: Share of presales recognised in the same year
assumptions.basis: Set to 1.0 because the presales history here is the recognised development revenue (property segment revenue), not marketing sales: ADCP has not disclosed marketing sales since FY2024 [S6] and no FY2025 annual report is reachable [S10]. One-to-one keeps the revenue build anchored on the actual P&L rather than on a presales figure we cannot evidence.

assumptions.label: Recurring revenue growth
assumptions.basis: Three GranDhika hotels (Jakarta, Medan, Semarang) generated Rp128.9bn in FY2024, up 11.75% year on year [S6]; we carry a 3% nominal rate as the mid-cycle run-rate for a hotel portfolio whose guests are business travellers.

assumptions.label: Development gross margin
assumptions.basis: The last actual is 9M-2026: cost of revenue Rp83.17bn on revenue Rp120.75bn gives a 31.1% gross margin for the property-led mix [S11]. We use that actual rather than a midpoint with the FY2024 figure, because the 9M-2026 accounts are the latest primary observation and the method card forbids an unexplained margin haircut. Held flat thereafter.

assumptions.label: Recurring gross margin
assumptions.basis: Hotel-segment gross margin: the FY2024 consolidated gross margin was 30.8% with the property segment at a loss-making level, so 30% is the level the three operating hotels have been able to hold through the downturn [S6]. Used both in the P&L and to capitalise the hotels in RNAV.

assumptions.label: Cap rate for investment property (RNAV)
assumptions.basis: House cap rate for Indonesian hotel and office assets: the BI policy rate of 5.75% from the macro deck plus a 4.25% property risk spread, giving 10%; used on the three GranDhika hotels' normalised gross profit to value the recurring business inside RNAV [S6].

assumptions.label: Target discount to RNAV
assumptions.basis: The 40-70% band is the house property-developer method (agents/methods/VAL_PROPERTY_DEVELOPER.md section 3), not a claim taken from S7 or S11: neither archived source states a discount band and the previous citation was wrong. We apply the band once, at 55% (above the midpoint), because the name-specific overlays sit at the adverse end: live PKPU petitions [S7], a 10.0004% public float, zero recorded traded value in the pack, a 9M-2026 loss of Rp68.33bn [S11] and a completion that depends on third-party funding [S4]. The discount is applied to the RNAV per share; there is no second liquidity discount on top, and the previous 45% x 70% stack is withdrawn.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Fixed in rupiah, not in ratio: 9M-2026 operating expense was Rp31.51bn [S11], i.e. Rp42.0bn annualised, in line with FY2023-FY2024 (Rp38.6bn and Rp39.6bn) and well below the FY2025 Rp73.4bn [S0], which carries the crisis-year one-offs. We hold Rp42.0bn flat for five years (the 82-person head-office and project-team structure) and let the ratio fall as revenue recovers; this is why FY2026E opex is 25.2% of revenue rather than the FY2025 37.2%.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(da, revenue)); asset-light shell, PP&E is Rp0.2bn

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Maintenance capex only: development spend sits in inventory, not PP&E (Rp0.17bn at FY2025), and completion of the stalled LRT City towers is funded by the Rp456bn Danantara facility rather than by the company's own capital expenditure [S11][S4].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Buyer advances fund construction, so operating working capital is negative (about minus Rp202bn on Rp197bn of revenue at FY2025); we hold -40% as the advances book unwinds through handovers [S11].

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: engine default: average of FY2023A, FY2024A, FY2025A (div(tax, pbt)); loss-making, so immaterial

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: The observed FY2025 interest charge of Rp54.2bn on Rp1,136bn of opening debt is 4.8% [S0], and we keep it: the 9.45% in the WACC block is the market cost of debt used to discount, not the cash rate this company actually pays on its subsidised and related-party facilities. The 9M-2026 loss is reconciled through an explicit other-charges line, not by inventing a higher interest rate [S11].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: The pack shows cash earning nothing while current liabilities exceed current assets; set to 4.5%, close to the 4.75% rupiah deposit rate implied by the macro deck, rather than the engine's 7% default. Interest income is immaterial (about Rp0.5bn a year) against a Rp54bn charge [S0].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: No new bank borrowing: lenders are not lending to a name with live PKPU petitions [S7]. The Rp456bn Danantara money is not booked as borrowing because the archived reports call it a "suntikan dana" to continue construction and do not state whether it is debt or equity [S4][S8]; booking it as debt would invent an interest charge, booking it as equity would invent a share issue. It funds completion spend that sits in inventory, below the P&L. The funding path is tested in the bear case and in section 4 of the report.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: FY2026E only: the 9M-2026 accounts show operating profit of about Rp6bn (revenue Rp120.75bn less cost of revenue Rp83.17bn less opex Rp31.51bn) against a net loss of Rp68.33bn, so about Rp74bn of below-the-line charges sit outside operating profit and the interest line over nine months [S11]. We carry Rp37.5bn of that (the annualised non-interest residual) in FY2026E and zero thereafter, because no driver is disclosed for it. It is not the FY2025 inventory write-down, which does not recur.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: engine default: minority interests are Rp0.5m on the balance sheet, so effectively nil

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero: no dividend has been paid since the FY2022 final (Rp1.17 per share) and equity is being consumed by losses, so a payout is neither funded nor likely [S0].

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: No rights issue assumed in the base case; a rescue rights issue is a bear-case risk, not a base assumption

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: House long-run nominal floor for an IDR reporting currency, below the macro deck CPI of 3.28% and real GDP of 5.29% (S0 pack macro block); used only in the cross-check DCF, not in the RNAV primary method.

challenges.challenge: The -81% is produced by discount architecture, not by the drivers named in the extreme_call justification: v0 11.375 = 0.75 x RNAV 8.97 + 0.25 x P/BV 18.61; RNAV 362.23 = 1,101 + 408.78 - 1,147.55 is a written-down book residual (book equity 350) that also double-counts cash (assets include it, net debt adds it back); the 45% 'RNAV discount' is then applied to that book base and a second 30% liquidity discount on top (0.55 x 0.70 = 0.385x book). Both bands sit outside their definition, and the 40-70% band is cited to S11/S7, which state neither band nor any developer discount.
challenges.answer: RNAV rebuilt with no double count: landbank leg is inventory 4,530 less other liabilities 3,601 plus other non-inventory net assets 352, so cash enters once through net debt and the hotels once at cap rate; RNAV 542.2 vs the old 362.2, per share 24.40 [S11][S6]. Discount applied once at the house band, disclosed with the engine's zero-ADTV overlay, and the 0.385x-book stack withdrawn. -81% survives at -82.7% because price 50 is 3.2x book, not because of architecture.

challenges.challenge: The P/BV 'cross-check' is knowingly invalid and still weighted 25%: own-history mean 1.131x (n=4) includes a post-collapse 2.7x observation the report itself calls 'a data artefact, not a valuation insight'. It adds Rp4.65 to v0 (41%) and about Rp2.2 to the Rp9 target, and at 1.13x it sits 2-7x house peer P/B (APLN 0.16x, AMAN 0.83x). A cross-check cannot be a co-driver, and a validated multiple would move value the other way.
challenges.answer: P/B weight zeroed (weights rnav 1.0, pbv 0.0); the own-history 1.131x is contaminated by the post-collapse observation and sits far above APLN/AMAN peer P/B, so the target is RNAV only [S0]. The cross-check is shown unweighted and the divergence explained in section 4, not co-driven.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E NP of -66.5 is arithmetically inconsistent with the 9M actual: 9M loss -68.3 [S11] plus Q4 revenue about 46.1 at the modelled 26% gross margin minus about 17 opex minus about 13.5 interest implies a Q4 loss of about Rp12bn, i.e. FY2026E about -80, not -66.5. The text's claim that -66.5 is 'the run-rate plus a normal fourth-quarter true-up' is therefore wrong — a true-up would widen the loss. The whole first forecast year also rests on one press summary of unaudited 9M figures, with no LK after Q2 2025 [S10].
challenges.answer: FY2026E rebuilt from the 9M actual: revenue 120.75, cost of revenue 83.17 (31.1% margin), opex 31.51 for nine months and the residual below-the-line charge implied by the loss of 68.33; FY2026E net profit is now -82.4, a Q4 loss rather than a profit [S11]. Prose corrected: a true-up widens the loss. Source quality of every FY+1 line stated.

challenges.challenge: The FY2025A anchor is vendor data, not a filing: fund record lines FY2025A revenue 197.34 and NP -2,107.21 come from the S0 data pack, but no FY2025 annual report is reachable and the latest LK is Q2 2025 [S10]. The -2,034.6 non-operating write-down, equity 417.7 and the inventory-at-NRV premise — the entire thesis — have no primary citation, and an 'A' (audited) suffix on an unaudited vendor year is misleading.
challenges.answer: FY2025A is vendor (S0) data, not a filing: no FY2025 AR/LK is archived and the IR page stops at Q2 2025 [S10]. The report now says so and widens uncertainty; the figures are corroborated arithmetically - equity 349.38 plus the 9M loss 68.33 equals the FY2025 equity 417.71, and FY2025 revenue 197.3 less 9M 165.54 leaves a plausible Q4 [S11][S0].

challenges.challenge: F2 (presales FY2025A = 170.338) and F3 (recurring_revenue FY2025A = 128.911) mis-state the year: S6 lines 677-678 read 'Properti 170.338 535.506 492.771 496.787 913.158' and 'Hotel 128.911 115.362 99.762 66.901 64.062', a five-year table running FY2024 back to FY2020 — 170.338 and 128.911 are FY2024, as the report's own section 1 confirms (170+129 = 300.3 = FY2024 revenue). The -80% FY2026E presales growth is therefore computed off an FY2024 base labelled FY2025A, and the hotel value capitalises FY2024 revenue.
challenges.answer: F2/F3 relabelled FY2024A with the verbatim segment quote and a new F23 adds the FY2023 column; the table is FY2024 back to FY2020 and 170.338 plus 128.911 equals the FY2024 revenue of 300.32 [S6]. F29/F30 are labelled carried anchors for the model's FY2025 slot because no FY2025 split is disclosed, and the implied FY2025 split (hotel about 129, property about 68) is stated.

challenges.challenge: The declared bridge leg is not applied and its probability is unsourced: 'Consumer refund settlement -158.0 x0.6' yields -94.8, but RNAV 362.23 equals 1,101 + 408.78 - 1,147.55 exactly, so the refund is nowhere in the method; the 0.6 probability has no source. Economically a refund is an asset-for-liability swap already inside the residual (buyer advances sit in the 3,601 other liabilities), so deducting it again would double count; if it were applied, the target falls to about Rp6.6.
challenges.answer: Refund leg removed from the bridge (bridge is now empty). Economically the refund is an asset-for-liability swap: buyer advances sit inside the 3,601 of other liabilities, so deducting 158 again is double counting, and the 0.6 probability had no source. It is carried as a bear-case and risk item instead [S5][S11].

challenges.challenge: The 2,400 undelivered units are called 'the whole investment case' but are not valued. The model recognises about Rp89-96bn of development revenue a year in FY2027-30 (about Rp390bn cumulative), which is about Rp163m per undelivered unit — below the construction cost of a mid-market LRT City flat and far below any plausible contracted ASP. No unit ASP, unit count or handover schedule appears in the model, so the December-2026 catalyst [S4][S5] exists only as narrative.
challenges.answer: Backlog valued explicitly in section 5: 2,400 sold-undelivered units, a sourced book cost per unit from inventory 4,530 over 9,839 units, and the model's FY2027E development revenue compared with it; no archived source states an ASP, which is said plainly. The bull case carries full handover on the December-2026 plan, and the advance-release point explains why the P&L does not repair cash [S3][S4][S11].

challenges.challenge: Asymmetric treatment of the two post-balance-sheet facts: the Rp456bn Danantara facility [S4], called 'the difference between completion and insolvency', is absent from the model and the bridge (no inflow, net_borrowing 0.000, capex 1.0%), while the refund claim is carried in the bridge. At 22,222m shares the facility is about Rp20/share against a Rp9 target. Meanwhile the base case has cash at -174.6 in FY2026E and parent equity -14.8 by FY2030E with no rights issue, no standstill and no default — an insolvent path that still carries a positive RNAV target.
challenges.answer: Danantara 456 stated as project funding whose instrument is not disclosed, so it is not booked as borrowing (that would invent interest) or equity (that would invent a share issue); it funds completion spend held in inventory [S4][S8]. Negative forecast cash is reconciled and disclosed as the non-cash recognition of revenue against pre-collected advances, not a funding forecast; the target is an asset value and the bear case is the no-facility/refund path.

challenges.challenge: opex_pct 37.2% of revenue contradicts the stated fixed cost base ('a fixed head-office and project-team structure of 82 employees'): with revenue down 15% the model's EBITDA margin improves from the -12.0% actual to -7.4% in FY2026E and -8.4% by FY2028E, which is exactly the 4.54pp calibration gap. That improvement has no source and is the only reason the EBITDA trajectory is not materially worse; if opex is fixed in Rp terms (about Rp73.4bn), FY2026E EBITDA is about -25, not -12.4.
challenges.answer: Opex is now fixed in rupiah at 42.0 (9M-2026 31.51 annualised) rather than the FY2025 37.2% ratio, and dev gross margin is the 9M actual 31.1%; FY2026E EBITDA is 9.4, not the -12.4 or -25 the two readings implied [S11][S0]. The calibration and drift flags are answered in qc_justifications with the 9M cost base as the source.

challenges.challenge: The scenario set is too narrow to be credible for a name with an insolvency path: base 13, bear 12, bull 15 — a plus/minus 15% band on a stock whose headline call is -81% — and the shocks are only presales plus/minus 10pp and RNAV discount plus/minus 10pp. The named bear risk (rescue rights issue/dilution, section 3) is not in the bear scenario, the refund risk sits in the bridge rather than the bear, and no scenario tests a successful PKPU or a suspension. The mirror is formally right but the dispersion does not reflect the stated risks.
challenges.answer: Scenarios widened: bear adds a rescue rights issue (share_change +0.15, the bound), a 15pp wider discount, weaker presales and a 5pp margin cut; bull mirrors presales, discount and margin. Probabilities 50/30/20 and the mirror asymmetry is justified in qc_justifications [S7][S0]. The 50% bear weighting sensitivity is stated in section 5.

challenges.challenge: The EARNINGS_QUALITY_FLAGS output contract is not met: no 3-year accruals ratio or cash-conversion trend (the year is dismissed as 'meaningless'), no IDX board/notation status (special monitoring board or B/E/L/M/S notation) despite the OJK sanction [S2], no related-party percentage of revenue or assets against the 90% parent — only 'a related-party web around the state parent' — and no PSAK 16 revaluation check on the hotel book before using equity as the valuation base.
challenges.answer: Output contract added in section 3: accruals substitute (equity bridge shows the loss is a non-cash write-down), cash-conversion deterioration, IDX board/notation check (no special monitoring or B/E/L/M/S found; OJK fine is presentation, optics-class) [S2], related-party assets 149.571 or a low single-digit share of assets [S6], and no PSAK 16 revaluation surplus in the equity note.

challenges.challenge: Typed numbers and unit errors: 'the macro deck has the policy rate at 575.0%' (100x error), 'USD/IDR at 18,350.0' (model fx 18,190), 'market capitalisation of Rp1,111,111,110,000.0' pasted raw, 'RpRp9' and 'RpRp19', '2,400 units units', '0.3 liquidity discount' beside 30.0%, and 'Rp0.0 per share' for the FY2022 dividend (Rp1.17 per share in the basis). The 22,222.2222m share count behind every per-share figure appears in no archived source and must be tied to the issued shares in the AR/LK; cash_yield 5% and kd 4.8% versus 9.45% in the WACC block are unreconciled.
challenges.answer: Typed numbers replaced with engine placeholders; policy rate and FX now use deck formats, the macro-capitalisation pasted value removed, duplicate Rp and unit labels fixed, and the dividend line uses the DPS placeholder [S0]. Share count is now tied to the AR by fact F28 (share capital 2,222,222m at Rp100 par) and the cost-of-debt/cash-yield basis reconciles 4.8% observed versus 9.45% market WACC input.

missing_bull_case.note: Two bull legs are narrated but not modelled: handover of the 2,400 undelivered units (model FY2027-30 development revenue ~Rp390bn, about Rp163m/unit — below build cost for an LRT City flat) and the Rp456bn Danantara facility, which at 22,222m shares is ~Rp20/share against a Rp9 target. Neither appears in cash flow or bridge.

missing_bear_case.note: Missing: a rescue rights issue or placement to meet the raised free-float floor (named in section 3 as a bear risk but absent from the bear scenario), and a quantification of a second inventory write-down if refunds cluster. Related-party extraction by the 90% parent is asserted ('a related-party web') but not quantified.

assumption_realism.note: opex_pct is held at 37.2% of revenue while section 3 calls the cost base a fixed 82-person head office — revenue -15% therefore improves EBITDA margin from -12.0% to -7.4% (the 4.54pp calibration gap), an unexplained cost cut. Dev gross margin 26.0% sits below the evidenced 9M-2026 31.1%. Hotel base 128.9 is FY2024, not FY2025.

evidence_and_citations.note: F2 presales 170.338 and F3 recurring 128.911 are the first two columns of the AR2024 five-year segment table (S6 lines 677-678, followed by 535.506 and 115.362, consistent with FY2024 to FY2020), yet labelled FY2025A; F22 (plan revenue 712) carries an 'A' suffix for a plan; the 40-70% discount band is cited to S11/S7, which do not state it; S5 and S8 have no date; FY2025A figures come only from the S0 data pack.

valuation_method_fit.note: The 'RNAV' is total assets 5,110 less other liabilities 3,601 less investment property, so it equals book equity plus cash (362 vs 350) — a written-down book residual, not the card's appraised land bank with a stated haircut; cash is counted in assets and added again via net debt. The P/BV 'cross-check' is the same book base at 1.13x, so the two methods disagree only on the multiple. BS dates are mixed (30 Jun cash/debt 11.65/1,159 vs 30 Sep assets 5,110).

bias_and_tone.note: Bearish framing goes beyond the evidence where it matters: 'a multiple of book that only makes sense if you believe the write-down was excessive' rests on a back-solved share count, and 'the market pays is not a market price' ignores that the last print is the IDX floor on zero volume. Credit: the loss arithmetic, funding gap and PKPU analysis are fair, and the conclusion survives a doubled bear (target moves about 4%).

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Own-history P/B of 1.13x is used as the cross-check multiple against house peer P/B of 0.16x (APLN) to 0.83x (AMAN) — 2-7x the sector — with no reconciliation. The BI path (5.75%) and the cap-rate build (5.75% + 4.25%) are consistent, but section 5 renders the policy rate as 575.0% and USD/IDR as 18,350 vs 18,190 in the model.

conservatism_audit.note: Below-last-actual or one-sided inputs: 45% RNAV discount taken at the 'narrow end' although the text says the float and PKPU argue for the middle of the band; dev gross margin at the midpoint rather than the evidenced 9M-2026 level; zero new borrowing; the refund leg carries a 0.6 probability in the bridge while the rescue inflow is zero-weighted; cash_yield cut to 5% from the 7% engine default. Not all one way: opex behaviour and the hotel gross-profit cap rate lean generous.

calibration.note: FY+1 EBITDA margin -7.4% against FY2025A actual -12.0%, gap 4.54pp, with no qc_justifications entry answering it — the improvement comes from opex scaling with a falling revenue line, contradicting the fixed-cost claim. Only the extreme_call BLOCK flag is justified, and its justification names qualitative drivers rather than the discount architecture that produces the -81%.

signoff.notes: Target chain reproduced to the rupiah: RNAV 542.230 (landbank 1,281 = inventory 4,530 - other liabilities 3,601 + other net assets 352; + investment property 408.78 at 10pct cap - net debt 1,147.5) / 22.2222m shares = 24.400; x 0.45 after the 55pct discount = 10.980; x 1.1675 COE roll = base 12.819; scenario weights 0.5/0.3/0.2 on base 12.819, bear 8.546, bull 17.093 = 12.392; x 0.70 zero-ADTV = 8.674 -> tp_final 9, tr -82.7pct. (The 8.82 in the brief weights the rounded 13/9/17 = 12.6 x 0.7; same Rp9.) No double count: cash enters once via net debt and the hotels once at cap value replacing the 203 book; RNAV equals 30 June book equity 335.3 + IP uplift 205.8 within about 1bn. Discount band is the house 40-70pct from agents/methods/VAL_PROPERTY_DEVELOPER.md, not S7/S11; 55pct + 30pct ADTV = 68.5pct, applied once, inside the band, and the report says so. Bias test: the SELL survives every band position - at 40pct and no overlay 24.4 x 0.60 x 1.1675 = 17.1 (-66pct), at zero discount 28.5 (-43pct), because price 50 is 2.05x RNAV and 3.2x book. So -82.7pct is a wide-band, floor-price value judgement, not a stacked bear; the header states the quote is the IDX floor and not an executable return. Base case ties to the 9M-2026 actual (revenue 120.75 annualises to about 161 vs FY2026E 166.85; opex fixed at 42.0; dev GM 31.1pct); no default haircuts. No broker rating, target or consensus in report or sources. Residual fixes next round, none call-changing: (1) Q1 open - s3 FY2027E prose omits the -8.6 cash-yield charge (EBIT 25.6 - interest 54.5 = -28.9 vs pbt -37.53) and the FY2022 dividend prints Rp0.0 against Rp1.17 in the basis; (2) Q2 open - macro policy rate and USD/IDR still cited [S6] instead of S0, and F5/F8 placeholders double the unit token (2,400 units units); (3) C5 fix incomplete - F29 presales FY2025A 170.338 is the FY2024 property segment number (duplicate of F2), so the presales growth base is FY2024; (4) mixed balance-sheet dates in net debt (Q5, about Rp0.2 of target) and the summary prints equity 335.3 beside F12 349.38; (5) Q3/Q4 - target Rp9 is below the IDX Rp50 minimum and the Danantara 456bn instrument treatment swings RNAV from 3.9 to 44.9 per share; state both in s5.

bias.note: SELL direction is right - price Rp50 is 2.05x the rebuilt RNAV of 542.2 (Rp24.40/sh) and 3.2x 9M-2026 book of 349.4 [S11] - but the target sits at the bottom of the admissible range and the -82.7% magnitude is overstated. A 55% RNAV cut (band midpoint) is applied to an anchor that is already a written-down book value (inventory at NRV after the FY2025 impairment, no appraisal uplift), then the 30% zero-ADTV overlay takes retained value to 31.5% of RNAV = a 68.5% total discount, versus the 40-70% house band [method card]. The return also divides by a price pinned at the IDX floor of Rp50 with zero traded value - S6 p.15 shows Rp50 in all four 2024 quarters with mcap Rp1,111,111,110,000 - so a further 83% fall is not realisable. Base-case operating drivers are not the problem: FY2026E EBITDA margin +17.6pp is sourced to the 9M-2026 actual (revenue 120.75 less cogs 83.17 less opex 31.51 = +6.07) [S11], opex is fixed in rupiah at the 9M run-rate [S11], revenue never regains FY2024 in the forecast and no dividend is paid. Rating unaffected: at the 40% band end the target would be about Rp12 and the call is still SELL.

recomputed.item: Target chain: 24.40 x 0.45 x 1.1675 = 12.82 base, x 0.70 ADTV overlay

findings.finding: Section 3 FY2027E bridge does not add: gross profit 67.5 less opex 41.9 leaves EBIT 25.6, and interest 54.5 then produces a pre-tax loss of -37.5. 25.6 - 54.5 = -28.9; the missing -8.6 is the cash_yield 4.5% charge on the negative FY2027E cash balance (-190.4) [S0]. The same section prints the FY2022 final dividend as Rp0.0 per share where the basis states Rp1.17.

Section 5 macro paragraph cites [S6] (Annual Report 2024) for the 5.75% policy rate and USD/IDR 18,350; the macro deck is the S0 pack and S6 is a FY2024 filing that cannot carry a 2026 rate or fx. Sections 3 and 5 still carry the duplicate unit artifacts C12 said were fixed: 2,400 units undelivered units; 9,839 units units; 2,400 units waiting buyers.

Target 9 sits at the bottom of the house 40-70% band: 55% RNAV cut plus the 30% zero-ADTV overlay retain 31.5% of RNAV. The RNAV anchor is itself a written-down book (inventory at NRV, no appraisal uplift), so the mid-band cut is applied to a distress value, and the overlay double-charges illiquidity in a name whose quote is already the exchange floor with zero traded value [S6 p.15]. The hotels are valued at a 10% cap on gross profit with no property opex or maintenance capex - the one generous leg.

The Rp456bn Danantara money is treated as net-neutral - not debt, not equity - because S4 calls it a suntikan dana and does not state the instrument [S4]. Defensible while undisbursed, but RNAV 542 assumes zero debt and zero dilution from it; on a loan treatment RNAV falls by 456 to Rp3.9 per share, an 84% cut.

Valuation net debt of 1,147.5 pairs 30 June 2026 pack cash (implying 11.5) with 30 September 2026 assets and liabilities [S0][S11]. Using 9M cash of 25.75 gives net debt 1,133.25, RNAV 556.5bn (Rp25.04/sh) and a target near Rp9.2.

flags.message: FY+1 ebitda margin moves +17.6pp from FY2025A: source the change
flags.justification: FY2025A EBITDA margin is -12.0% because the year carried the crisis cost base (opex Rp73.4bn on revenue Rp197.3bn) [S0]; FY2026E is +5.6%. The move is sourced to the 9M-2026 accounts: revenue Rp120.75bn less cost of revenue Rp83.17bn less operating expense Rp31.51bn leaves about Rp6bn of operating profit for nine months, which annualises positive on a lower cost base [S11]. The calibrated re-pricing at FY2025 revenue therefore does not hold because the cost base itself changed in the 9M actual, not because we assume operating leverage.

flags.message: a.opex_pct moves -10.3pp from FY2026E to FY2030E: source the change or hold it
flags.justification: The ratio falls 10.3pp because the rupiah opex is held at Rp42.0bn (the 9M-2026 Rp31.51bn annualised [S11]), not because of an assumed efficiency. Revenue recovers from the handover cycle while the fixed 82-person head office does not, so the ratio mechanically declines. The FY2025 Rp73.4bn is not the run-rate: it carries crisis-year one-offs and is 86% above FY2024 [S0]. Holding the ratio would imply opex rising with revenue with no sourced cost plan.

flags.message: bear and bull shock different drivers (bear only ['a.share_change'], bull only [])
flags.justification: The bear carries one driver the bull does not: a rescue rights issue (a.share_change +0.15, the upper bound). That asymmetry is sourced and one-sided: a developer with negative free cash flow, negative EBITDA in FY2025 [S0] and a Rp349bn equity base cannot buy back stock, while a rights issue is the standard rescue route for an IDR name with live PKPU petitions [S7]. All other drivers (presales growth, RNAV discount, development gross margin) are mirrored one-for-one.

flags.message: expected return -83%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: The return is large because the price is, not because the discount is stacked. Corrected RNAV is Rp542bn or Rp24.40 per share (book equity Rp349.38bn plus a Rp206bn investment-property revaluation [S11][S6]); the house property band cuts that once at 55% and the zero-ADTV overlay takes it to about a third of RNAV, still inside the 40-70% band. The price of Rp50 is 2.05x that RNAV and 3.2x book, on a company with a 9M-2026 loss of Rp68.33bn [S11], a live PKPU petition [S7] and a 10% float [S6]. No archived document supports the write-down being excessive, so the equity is expensive on every asset measure, not only on the band.
